stories.title: Knighthead Lends $63M or Doral, Fla. Industrial Portfolio Buy
stories.excerpt: Midtown Capital Partners has sealed $62.92 million of acquisition financing to fund its purchase of 13 urban-infill, small-bay industrial assets in Doral, Fla., Commercial Observer has learned. Knighthead Funding provided the loan for Midtown’s $86 million off-market acquisition of the 290,000-square-foot portfolio spanning 13.33 acres, according to the lender. Midtown purchased the properties from Wes Realty in August at a near-record industrial sales price for Miami-Dade County, The Real Deal previously reported. The 13 properties were developed and assembled over the last 30 years, according to Knighthead, which originated the deal with a team led by Jonathan Daniel, Alexandra Wiggins and Joseph Marraccini. “This transaction epitomizes what we look for when financing a deal — an attractive collection of assets with significant upside in an excellent infill location,” Wiggins, vice president at Knighthead Funding, said in a statement. The properties, which are located west of Miami within a mile of Miami International Airport, benefit from strong demand for small-bay industrial properties in South Florida, where vacancy rates are below 3 percent, according to Knighthead. Arrow Real Estate Advisors arranged the debt with a team consisting of Morris Betesh, Morris Dabbah and Zach Strauss. “Urban-infill portfolios like this come around once in a lifetime,” Betesh, founder and managing partner at Arrow, said in a statement. “We’ve seen the small-bay industrial sector mature significantly over the last several years, and this acquisition, along with the capital markets’ reception to the transaction, is another indication of how increasingly institutional the asset class has become.” Midtown Capital Partners did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Knighthead Funding closed $62.92M acquisition loan for Midtown Capital's 13-property industrial portfolio in Doral, FL
290,000 SF, 13.33-acre infill portfolio near Miami International Airport sold for ~$86M in August 2024
Urban small-bay industrial assets in Miami-Dade County reflect strong last-mile logistics demand near airport hub
stories.summary: Midtown Capital purchased a 290,000-square-foot, 13-property industrial portfolio in Doral, Florida for approximately $86 million in an off-market transaction, with Knighthead Funding providing $62.92 million in acquisition financing. The properties are located within one mile of Miami International Airport and were assembled over 30 years. The near-record sales price for Miami-Dade industrial reflects strong investor appetite for infill logistics assets positioned for e-commerce and international trade.
stories.impact: Strong institutional capital availability and aggressive pricing in Miami industrial signals robust last-mile logistics demand tied to airport proximity and port access. For multifamily developers in South Florida, this reflects broader Miami metro economic strength and population/jobs growth that supports concurrent residential demand; infill land near airport/port logistics hubs may face increasing competition from logistics investors, potentially elevating land costs in those submarkets.

stories.title: Lucrum Realty Acquires 50K-SF Lewisville Retail Center
stories.excerpt: Lake Park Plaza, a 50,511-square-foot multi-tenant retail center at 359 Lake Park Road in Lewisville, Texas, has traded hands. Phil Rosenfeld of Lee & Associates Dallas-Fort Worth represented the buyer, an affiliate of Lucrum Realty. While the sales price was not disclosed, the listed sale price for Lake Park Plaza was $7,250,000. Built in 1985, Lake Park Plaza is on the corner of Lake Park Road and Oakridge Boulevard, half a mile from Lake Park — the City of Lewisville’s 662-acre lakefront park, with two golf courses, a marina, boat ramps, an RV campground and swim beaches. The center is anchored by a fuel and convenience operator, with automotive service, an event center, and a mix of food, retail, personal-service and professional-office tenants. Lucrum Realty has begun a program of improvements at the property, including new monument and tenant signage, and a refreshed identity for the center. Lee & Associates has been retained to handle leasing at Lake Park Plaza. The post Lucrum Realty Acquires 50K-SF Lewisville Retail Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Lucrum Realty acquired 50,511 SF retail center in Lewisville, TX for listed price of $7.25M
Lake Park Plaza, built 1985, anchored by fuel/convenience, automotive, event center; near 662-acre lakefront park
Buyer initiated capital improvement program: new signage, branding refresh, active leasing push via Lee & Associates
stories.summary: Lucrum Realty acquired Lake Park Plaza, a 50,511-square-foot multi-tenant retail center in Lewisville, Texas, at a listed price of $7.25 million. Built in 1985 and located at Lake Park Road and Oakridge Boulevard near the city's 662-acre lakefront park, the center is anchored by a fuel/convenience operator with automotive service, event space, and mixed retail/professional tenants. The buyer has launched a capital improvement and leasing program.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. Retail acquisition and repositioning in Lewisville signals stabilizing consumer demand in Dallas-Fort Worth suburbs, but does not directly affect residential supply, financing, or development costs. Incremental indication of broader DFW market activity.

stories.title: U.S. Apartment Rents Decline for 37th Consecutive Month
stories.excerpt: The national median asking rent for studio, one- and two-bedroom apartments across the 50 largest U.S. metropolitan areas fell 0.9% year over year to $1,699, according to the Realtor.com August Rental Report. This marks the 37th consecutive month of annual declines. The median asking rent is now $65, or 3.7%, below its summer 2022 peak, while remaining $227, or 15.4%, above August 2019 levels. The continued decline translates into meaningful savings for renters compared with the market’s recent peak, even as renting costs remain elevated compared with pre-pandemic levels. “Renters are entering the fall with more choices and more negotiating power than they had at the height of the rental market,” said Jiayi Xu, senior economist at Realtor.com. “Rents are still above pre-pandemic levels, but the combination of continued year-over-year declines, new supply and a growing share of listings with concessions is creating more opportunities for renters to find better deals. We expect the typical seasonal slowdown in monthly rents this fall, with year-over-year declines likely to continue as rental supply works through the market.” The post U.S. Apartment Rents Decline for 37th Consecutive Month appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: U.S. median asking rent fell 0.9% YoY to $1,699 in August across 50 largest metros; 37 consecutive months of decline
Rents now $65 (3.7%) below summer 2022 peak but $227 (15.4%) above August 2019 pre-pandemic baseline
Realtor.com notes renters gaining bargaining power, rising concessions, and new supply absorption continuing through fall
stories.summary: The national median asking rent for one- and two-bedroom apartments fell 0.9% year-over-year to $1,699 across the 50 largest U.S. metros in August, marking the 37th consecutive month of annual declines. Rents have retreated $65 (3.7%) from the summer 2022 peak while remaining $227 (15.4%) above August 2019 levels. Analyst commentary indicates sustained oversupply, growing tenant concessions, and expectation of continued YoY declines into fall as new inventory works through the market.
stories.impact: Extended rent declines signal persistent overbuilding and weakening demand relative to supply in most major markets, pressuring yield assumptions and valuations on new apartment starts. This environment raises development risk for non-stabilized and non-differentiated product; developers must focus on high-barrier, supply-constrained submarkets or premium positioning to justify new construction costs and secure attractive pre-leasing. The 37-month decline streak suggests demand recovery will be slow—underwriting must assume further modest pressure before stabilization.

stories.title: Texas People & Companies, September 18, 2026
stories.excerpt: Dallas-based Mohr Partners named 20-year industry veteran Dodie Williams as Managing Partner of Project Management Services. In this newly created leadership role, Williams will oversee the firm’s national project management practice, working with corporate occupiers to manage buildouts, relocations and capital improvement projects across their real estate portfolios. Williams brings more than 20 years of commercial real estate and project management experience to Mohr Partners. Throughout her career, she has held leadership positions with several firms, including JLL, Macro Consultants, Trammell Crow and Jackson Cross Partners. Dallas-based CenterPoint Commercial Companies launched CenterPoint Commercial Capital, a new capital markets division focused on commercial real estate debt and equity placement nationwide. As part of the expansion, CenterPoint has recruited seasoned commercial real estate finance professionals Ari Raskas, founder of ARZ Realty Capital, and Matthew Sheard, formerly of Marcus & Millichap Capital Corporation, to spearhead the new platform. The Multifamily Group (TMG) brokered the sale of Northwind Apartments, a 71-unit multifamily community located along Interstate 35 in Waco, Texas. Built in 1978, Northwind is located less than one mile from Texas State Technical College. Jon Krebbs represented the undisclosed seller, while Angel Flores sourced the buyer, also undisclosed. The transaction employed a loan assumption and a preferred equity structure to bridge the gap between the seller’s pricing objectives and the realities of today’s capital markets. Berkadia announced the sale of 220 & 230 West Alabama, two multifamily properties totaling 131 units in Houston, Texas. The Berkadia Houston Investment Sales team was led by Kyle Whitney and included Chris Curry, Jeffrey Skipworth, Chris Young, and Joey Rippel, and Tucker Fama. stories.title: Florida People & Companies, September 18, 2026
stories.excerpt: Scott Florio has joined Newmark as Regional Project Management Leader for Florida. Based in Orlando, Florio will establish and lead Newmark’s Project Management presence across Tampa, Orlando and Jacksonville, while leveraging Newmark’s statewide business and relationships to support clients throughout Florida, including Miami, Fort Lauderdale, West Palm Beach, Naples and Fort Myers. He will collaborate with brokers and professionals across the state to deliver integrated capital project solutions for occupiers, developers and investors. Most recently, he served as Director of Project Management for CBRE | Turner & Townsend’s North Florida Region. The Palomar Group brokered the sale of Port Orange Plaza, a retail shopping center located in Port Orange, Florida. Port Orange Plaza is anchored by Human-Conviva Care Center and Modern Concepts, and sits along S Ridgewood Ave, a corridor that sees more than 52,000 vehicles per day. The center was 81% occupied at closing, with in-place rents below market, offering the incoming ownership a clear value-add opportunity. The seller was M&P Shopping Centers. WareSpace, an operator of micro-bay warehouse space, spent $20 million on industrial acquisitions in Miami Gardens, Florida. The 100,000-square-foot property will be converted into flexible warehouse units, expected to serve more than 125 small businesses, along one of Miami-Dade County’s busiest commercial corridors. WareSpace will reposition the properties as flexible, move-in-ready warehouse units, typically ranging from 200 to 2,000 square feet.  Miramar Park of Commerce, the largest locally owned and managed business park in South Florida, reports the company has closed more than 330,000 square feet of healthcare-related lease renewals so far in 2026. stories.title: Ares Management, PSP Investments Form $2.4B U.S. Logistics Partnership
stories.excerpt: Ares Management is diving deeper into the waters of U.S. logistics. The $670 billion private equity powerhouse announced Wednesday that it has formed a joint venture with Canada’s Public Sector Pension Investment Board (PSP Investments) to invest up to $2.4 billion into the development and acquisition of U.S. logistics facilities. Ares plans to combine its vertically integrated logistics real estate platform, Marq Logistics, with PSP’s scaled capital to invest into “high-conviction markets” and “strategically placed logistics facilities,” according to a release. Dave Fazekas, head of North America logistics at Ares Real Estate, noted in a statement that his firm was motivated to invest into domestic logistics hubs due to resurgent onshoring trends, growth of digital infrastructure construction, and the economy’s ongoing reliance on e-commerce. “We are proud to expand Ares’ long-standing relationship with PSP Investments as we leverage our collective scale and experience to identify compelling deployment opportunities and deliver value for tenants, communities and investors,” he said. The joint venture already plans to invest in a 5.2 million-square-foot seed portfolio of 14 assets in California, Texas and New Jersey. Laurence Bastien, managing director of real estate investments for the Americas at PSP Investments, emphasized in a statement that the U.S. logistics sector is currently defined by “durable demand drivers and structurally constrained supply,” and the partnership with Ares provides his firm with an operating platform that will “drive value at the asset level.” “Best-in-class operators, in sectors where our conviction is strongest — that is what our real estate strategy is built around, and this joint venture has both,” added Bastien. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Ares Management and PSP Investments (Canada) launched $2.4B joint venture for U.S. logistics development and acquisition
Ares combining vertically integrated Marq Logistics platform with PSP's scaled capital to target 'high-conviction' logistics markets
Investment thesis driven by onshoring trends, digital infrastructure growth, and sustained e-commerce demand
stories.summary: Ares Management and Canada's Public Sector Pension Investment Board (PSP Investments) have formed a $2.4 billion joint venture to develop and acquire U.S. logistics facilities, combining Ares' Marq Logistics vertical platform with PSP's institutional capital. The partnership targets high-conviction logistics markets and strategically positioned facilities, motivated by onshoring momentum, digital infrastructure growth, and sustained e-commerce reliance. The deal reflects continued institutional appetite for logistics as a defensive, income-generating asset class.
stories.impact: Large institutional logistics capital deployment signals confidence in onshoring and last-mile demand persistence, which will intensify competition for logistics-proximate infill land in gateway and secondary metros. This increases land acquisition costs in submarkets near ports, airports, and e-commerce fulfillment corridors, potentially squeezing multifamily development feasibility on adjacent sites and raising land cost basis for developers seeking infill positions in logistics-heavy corridors (e.g., Inland Empire, Atlanta, Dallas).

stories.title: Wells Fargo Refis Long Island City Apartments With $115M Fannie Mae Loan
stories.excerpt: An affiliate of Rockrose Development has secured $115 million of agency-backed debt to refinance a newly completed multifamily complex in Long Island City, Commercial Observer has learned. Wells Fargo Multifamily Capital closed the Fannie Mae-backed loan for Rockrose’s 301-unit Eagle Lofts Collection, Phase 2, which opened last year in Long Island City’s Court Square neighborhood. The 19-story building on 43-14 Queens Street shares a lobby and amenities with Rockrose’s adjacent 790-unit Eagle Lofts Collection, Phase 1 tower. Avison Young negotiated the debt with a tri-state debt and equity finance team consisting of Scott Singer, Andy Singer, Kevin Swartz and Kathleen McSharry. “Long Island City remains one of the region’s most compelling multifamily markets, driven by strong residential demand, extraordinarily convenient transportation, and ongoing neighborhood growth,” Scott Singer, principal at Avison Young, said in a statement. “Phase 2 has further elevated Rockrose’s earlier Phase 1 of the Eagle Lofts Collection.” Seventy percent of apartments at Eagle Lofts Collection, Phase 2 are market rate with 30 percent of the units designated as affordable housing. The property’s amenities include a spa with saunas, a bowling alley, a golf simulator and a rooftop pool. Wells Fargo originated the loan with a team led by Pete Cannava, head of multifamily capital and community lending and Investment; Philip Maniscalco, head of production for multifamily capital; and Brian Antonuccio, head of East Coast production. “With 301 new residences, nearly a third of them affordable, Eagle Lofts Collection, Phase 2 meaningfully expands housing access in Long Island City,” Maniscalco said in a statement. Richard Brancato, chief operating officer at Rockrose, said in a statement, the transaction “reflects the strength” of its “long-standing relationships” with Wells Fargo and Avison Young. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Rockrose Development closed $115M Fannie Mae refi via Wells Fargo for 301-unit Eagle Lofts Collection Phase 2, Long Island City
19-story newly completed building at 43-14 Queens Street shares lobby/amenities with adjacent 790-unit Phase 1 (1,091 total units combined)
Agency debt availability and strong underwriting on recently delivered LIC multifamily reflect sustained investor confidence in Queens market
stories.summary: Rockrose Development secured $115 million in agency-backed financing from Wells Fargo (Fannie Mae) to refinance the newly completed 301-unit Eagle Lofts Collection, Phase 2 in Long Island City. The 19-story building at 43-14 Queens Street shares amenities with the adjacent 790-unit Phase 1, creating a combined 1,091-unit complex in the Court Square neighborhood. The refinancing reflects strong lender appetite for stabilized multifamily in Long Island City driven by transit access and neighborhood growth.
stories.impact: Fannie Mae refi availability and competitive pricing on newly delivered LIC apartments confirm sustained institutional capital appetite for Queens multifamily and validates strong absorption/demand in Long Island City submarkets. This supports development economics for future LIC infill projects and suggests lower refinance risk, improving overall project returns and enabling developers to underwrite LIC starts at tighter cap rates; however, tight market conditions and high land costs in LIC may limit new-start feasibility unless rents continue to stabilize above current $1,699 national median.

stories.title: Borough Developers Closes on $84M Sale of Downtown Brooklyn Development Site
stories.excerpt: Brooklyn-based Borough Developers has acquired a major mixed-use development site in Downtown Brooklyn, right across from the new retail project at a former Macy’s, Commercial Observer has learned. The firm acquired 485 Fulton Street and 147 Lawrence Street — a 33,153-square-foot site known as the Bridge & Fulton Development Site — from ICER Real Estate for $83.5 million, according to JLL, which brokered the deal for both sides. Borough Developers secured an $85 million acquisition and pre-development loan from BridgeCity Capital for the deal. “The transaction closed in just 16 days, underscoring our ability to move quickly and execute under tight deadlines,” EJ Ehrlich, director of originations at BridgeCity, said in a statement to CO. “This transaction reflects our continued ability to structure and execute complex financing solutions for high-quality development sites across New York City.” Last month, Shimon Kleinman, co-founder of Borough Developers, filed plans with the New York City Department of Buildings to build a trio of 99-unit residential buildings on the site, meaning the developer is likely trying to utilize the state’s 485-x tax abatement program. That program comes with steeper construction wage requirements for projects of 100 units or more. Kleinman’s initial filing would see a total of 297 housing units built on the site, but BridgeCity said the building is set to comprise a total of 468 residential units, commercial space and amenities. JLL, which said the planned number of units is subject to change, said the project will include four buildings comprising retail on the ground floor and residential units above. The development site has 350,000 buildable square feet. The existing 139,438-square-foot building on the property — currently home to a barber shop — will be demolished to make way for the new housing, according to JLL. bullets: Borough Developers acquired 33,153 SF mixed-use dev site in Downtown Brooklyn (485 Fulton & 147 Lawrence St) for $83.5M

The Bridge & Fulton Development Site is located adjacent to a new retail conversion from a former Macy's building. The rapid 16-day closing underscores developer and lender appetite for high-quality Brooklyn infill opportunities.
stories.impact: Quick execution and meaningful pre-development financing availability for Downtown Brooklyn mixed-use sites signals sustained developer/lender confidence in Brooklyn residential demand and neighborhood transformation trajectory. The adjacent Macy's conversion provides anchor retail demand and signals continued commercial/retail repositioning around the site; this validates longer-term residential absorption and justifies premium pricing on development sites, but also reflects intensifying competition for scarce Brooklyn infill land, pushing acquisition costs higher and tightening margin tolerance for developers unless residential pre-leasing or long-term commercial anchors are secured early.

stories.title: Scheels Building 300K-SF Littleton Store, Town Okays Tax Breaks
stories.excerpt: SCHEELS announced this week that it is building a 300,000-square-foot store in Littleton. The store is planned as an anchor retailer alongside Costco at the new Mineral Place development. The flagship sporting goods store spans over 80 specialty shops under one roof, including golf, baseball and softball, archery, bicycles, ski equipment and fishing gear. And yes, a 60-foot Ferris wheel, as well. Concurrently, Littleton officials approved a 30-year tax incentive deal that will ease the property tax burden of the massive retailer. As part of the approved deal, Scheels would receive a 54.67% sales tax refund over that period. Littleton would retain 40% of the sales tax collected. In return for the incentives, Scheels must agree to obtain its certificate of occupancy within four years. The company plans to hire 500 workers. Construction is anticipated to start in the first quarter of 2027 with an opening anticipated in the spring of 2029. The post Scheels Building 300K-SF Littleton Store, Town Okays Tax Breaks appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Scheels confirmed 300,000 SF flagship store in Littleton, CO at Mineral Place development alongside Costco anchor

stories.summary: Scheels announced a 300,000-square-foot flagship sporting goods store in Littleton, Colorado as an anchor at the Mineral Place development alongside Costco. The Littleton municipal government approved a 30-year tax incentive providing Scheels with a 54.67% sales tax refund while retaining 40% of collected taxes. The retailer commits to hiring 500 workers and obtaining certificate of occupancy within four years, with construction starting Q1 2027 and opening planned for spring 2029.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. Large retail anchor and municipal tax incentives signal government interest in anchored mixed-use/retail development in suburban Denver (Littleton), but story does not address residential components or broader Littleton housing supply/demand dynamics. If Mineral Place includes multifamily, strong retail anchors support higher rents/occupancy; however, no residential details provided. Indirect signal of continued Denver metro suburban development activity and municipal willingness to subsidize large retailers.

stories.title: Capital Insight Acquires Hudson Yards Hotel Property in Foreclosure Auction
stories.excerpt: Capital Insight has acquired a former hotel with retail and parking in Manhattan’s Hudson Yards for somewhere between $68 million and $71.3 million, according to court records. Investment banking business Capital Insight — the former lender and debt holder on the property — took ownership of the 12-story building at 511 Ninth Avenue through a foreclosure auction. The auction occurred after Assa Properties fell into financial troubles associated with the property and the site went to special servicing through CW Capital Asset Management. Capital Insight and CW Capital did not immediately respond to requests for comment. PincusCo first reported the foreclosure auction, saying Capital Insight was expected to use the property as a cash-flowing asset with its six commercial condominiums. Assa planned the Ninth Avenue development as a combination hotel-multifamily property branded as Galerie515 Hotel & Condominium Residences when construction first began in 2012. The residential portion was also named Lana at some point, and the Cassa Hotel Times Square portion closed in 2020. A new steakhouse named Vida Steakhouse is set to open in the retail space at 511 Ninth Avenue next year, but it’s unclear if that lease will proceed under new ownership. Assa Properties, owned by the Assa family and led by founder Solly Assa, could not be reached for comment. The most recent property records linking the ownership to the Assa family date back to 2014, with filings linked to Cassa Capital, one of Assa’s other organizations, through an address at 410 Park Avenue. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Capital Insight acquired 12-story former hotel at 511 Ninth Avenue, Hudson Yards via foreclosure auction for $68M–$71.3M
Property originally planned as hotel-multifamily hybrid (Galerie515 Hotel & Condominium Residences); hotel component (Cassa Hotel) closed 2020
Foreclosure reflects pandemic-era hotel distress; new owner taking possession of mixed-use property with six commercial condominiums and ground-floor retail
stories.summary: Capital Insight acquired a 12-story mixed-use property at 511 Ninth Avenue in Manhattan's Hudson Yards for approximately $68–71.3 million through a foreclosure auction. Originally conceived as a hybrid hotel-multifamily property (Galerie515 Hotel & Condominium Residences), the project suffered financial distress under previous owner Assa Properties, with the hotel component (Cassa Hotel Times Square) closing in 2020. The property comprises six commercial condominiums, retail space, parking, and will operate under new ownership as a cash-flowing mixed-use asset.
stories.impact: Hudson Yards hotel foreclosure underscores persistent pandemic-era hotel sector weakness and indicates selective opportunity to acquire distressed mixed-use sites in prime Manhattan submarkets at reduced basis. For multifamily developers, this signals potential conversion/repositioning upside on underperforming hotel-residential hybrids in high-cost markets; however, Hudson Yards' oversupply of office and weak hotel demand may limit residential conversion upside unless strong office-to-residential conversion tax incentives (like recent NYC programs) become available. Foreclosure activity suggests cap rates may remain elevated for hospitality-linked properties, creating tactical acquisition windows for developers with repositioning expertise.
